scope: Bexar, Comal & Guadalupe counties (San Antonio region): healthcare, mental health, school/childcare, employment, legal (plus related local housing, utility and transit help)

records.name: The Center for Health Care Services (Bexar County Local Mental Health Authority)
records.organization: The Center for Health Care Services
records.description_en: Mental health and substance use treatment for adults and children in Bexar County. Also offers intellectual and developmental disability services, peer support, and supportive housing help.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Bexar County residents who need mental health, substance use, or developmental disability services.
records.how_to_apply: Call the routine appointments line at 1-833-501-2427 to set up care. In a crisis, call the 24/7 crisis line.
records.notes: CHCS is the Local Mental Health Authority for Bexar County. Treats anxiety, depression, PTSD, bipolar disorder, schizophrenia, postpartum depression, and alcohol/drug use.

records.name: CHCS 24/7 Crisis Line
records.organization: The Center for Health Care Services
records.description_en: A phone line for anyone in Bexar County having a mental health or substance use crisis. Trained staff can talk with you and connect you to help.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Anyone in Bexar County in a mental health crisis, or someone calling for them.
records.how_to_apply: Call (210) 223-7233 or 1-800-316-9241. If someone is in immediate danger, call 911.
records.notes: Toll-free alternate: 1-800-316-9241. The 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline is also available nationally.

records.name: Hill Country MHDD Centers - Comal County Mental Health
records.organization: Hill Country Mental Health and Developmental Disabilities Centers
records.description_en: Public mental health clinic in New Braunfels for adults and children. The agency also offers substance use services, crisis care, and developmental disability services.
records.eligibility_summary_en: People living in Comal County who need mental health care.
records.how_to_apply: Call the Comal County Mental Health clinic at (830) 620-6221. For a crisis, call 1-877-466-0660 any time.
records.notes: Hill Country MHDD serves Comal County among 19 Hill Country counties. Intellectual/developmental disability (LIDDA) office is at 358 Landa Street, Suite 100, (830) 625-7394. Main agency line: (830) 792-3300.

records.name: Hill Country MHDD 24/7 Crisis Hotline
records.organization: Hill Country Mental Health and Developmental Disabilities Centers
records.description_en: A crisis phone line for people in a mental health emergency in the Hill Country area, including Comal County. It connects to crisis staff and the Mobile Crisis Outreach Team.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Anyone in the Hill Country MHDD service area, including Comal County, having a mental health crisis.
records.how_to_apply: Call 1-877-466-0660. If someone is in immediate danger, call 911.
records.notes: Service area also includes Bandera, Blanco, Edwards, Gillespie, Hays, Kendall, Kerr, Kimble, Kinney, Llano, Mason, Medina, Menard, Real, Schleicher, Sutton, Uvalde and Val Verde counties.

records.name: Bluebonnet Trails Community Services - Seguin
records.description_en: Public mental health, substance use, and crisis services in Seguin. It also offers autism help, early childhood intervention, disability services, and veteran peer support.
records.eligibility_summary_en: People in Guadalupe County who need mental health, substance use, or developmental disability services.
records.how_to_apply: Call 1-844-309-6385 (7:30 a.m.-5:30 p.m.) for appointments. For a crisis, call 1-800-841-1255 any time.
records.hours: Appointment line 7:30 a.m. - 5:30 p.m.; crisis line 24/7
records.notes: 24/7 crisis line: 1-800-841-1255. Bluebonnet Trails serves several Central Texas counties; the Seguin office serves Guadalupe County.

records.name: Clarity Child Guidance Center
records.description_en: Mental health care for children and teens, including 24/7 crisis help, hospital care, day programs, and outpatient therapy.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Children ages 3 to 17. Families are served no matter their ability to pay.
records.how_to_apply: Call (210) 616-0300 or walk in to the crisis center any time.
records.cost: Serves families regardless of ability to pay; financial aid available
records.notes: Walk-ins welcome for crisis assessment 24/7.

records.name: CentroMed Community Health Centers
records.description_en: Community health centers offering family medicine, children's care, women's health, dental, eye care, pharmacy, lab work, behavioral health, and WIC. Fees can be lowered based on income.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Open to everyone. A sliding fee based on income and family size is available, and no one is turned away for inability to pay.
documents_needed: Photo ID (driver's license, government ID, resident card, birth certificate, or passport)
Proof of address (utility bill or any mail with your name and address)
Proof of income for the last 30 days (pay stubs, tax return if self-employed, Social Security or unemployment letters, TANF/SNAP papers)
Proof of family members (birth certificates or Medicaid/CHIP/SNAP/WIC papers)
records.how_to_apply: Call (210) 922-7000 for an appointment. To apply for the sliding fee, apply online or call (210) 334-3745 to meet with an eligibility specialist.
records.hours: Scheduling line Monday-Friday, 8:00 AM - 5:00 PM; appointment support 24/7 (after hours, option 3)
records.cost: Sliding fee scale based on income; no one denied for inability to pay
records.notes: Address shown is the administration office; eligibility page says in-person help is at six locations across San Antonio and New Braunfels. Interpretation available at all locations. Also helps people enroll in ACA Marketplace coverage.

records.name: CommuniCare Health Centers - San Antonio
records.description_en: Community health centers with 20+ clinics in San Antonio offering primary care for kids and adults, women's health, dental, behavioral health, pharmacy, and WIC. Uninsured patients can get a sliding fee discount.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Open to everyone. The sliding fee discount is for families with income under 200% of the federal poverty level.
documents_needed: Photo ID (state ID, driver's license including foreign license, school ID, or passport)
Insurance card, if you have one
List of current medicines
records.how_to_apply: New patients call (210) 233-7000 to set up a first visit. For the sliding fee discount or help with Medicaid/Marketplace, call the Medical Eligibility team at (210) 233-7076.
records.cost: Sliding fee discount for uninsured patients under 200% FPL
records.notes: Address is the corporate campus; clinic list at https://communicaresa.org/locations/san-antonio-locations/. Payment by debit/credit card; cash not accepted. Also has a Retama (Selma) campus.

records.name: CommuniCare Health Centers - New Braunfels Campus
records.description_en: Community health center in New Braunfels offering sick visits, adult and child care, senior care, chronic disease care, and shots.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Open to new patients. Sliding fee discount for families with income under 200% of the federal poverty level.
documents_needed: Photo ID
Insurance card, if you have one
List of current medicines
records.how_to_apply: Call (210) 233-7000 to book, or book online.
records.cost: Sliding fee discount for uninsured patients under 200% FPL
records.notes: Accepting new patients. Sliding fee questions: (210) 233-7076.

records.name: CareLink
records.description_en: A financial help program that makes care at University Health cheaper for uninsured Bexar County families. It is not insurance.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Bexar County residents with income at or below 250% of the federal poverty level who do not have and cannot get health insurance.
records.how_to_apply: Fill out the CareLink enrollment application online (English or Spanish), then schedule an enrollment appointment. Call CareLink Member Services at (210) 358-3350 with questions.
records.notes: Spanish application: https://forms.uhstx.com/CLMemberApp-SP.html. An appointment is required to enroll or renew. Call to ask which documents to bring.

records.name: Metro Health Immunization Clinic
records.description_en: Low-cost vaccines for children and uninsured adults. Children can get shots through Texas Vaccines for Children and adults through the Adult Safety Net program.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Children 18 and under who are uninsured, underinsured, on Medicaid/CHIP, or Native American; adults 19+ without insurance.
records.how_to_apply: Call (210) 207-8790 to make an appointment. Appointments are required.
records.hours: Monday - Friday 8 a.m. - 3 p.m. (closed 12-1 p.m. for lunch); may close early if full
records.cost: Children: $13.75 admin fee per visit (TVFC). Uninsured adults: $22 per vaccine (Adult Safety Net).
records.notes: Accepts Medicaid and Community First / Superior Health CHIP only; private insurance is not accepted.

records.name: Metro Health STI/HIV Clinic and PrEP Clinic
records.description_en: Walk-in testing and treatment for sexually transmitted infections, plus a PrEP clinic to help prevent HIV.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Anyone who needs STI testing or treatment or HIV prevention. The PrEP team helps people regardless of their finances.
records.how_to_apply: Walk in to the clinic. For PrEP, call (210) 207-7292 to schedule; walk-ins accepted.
records.notes: PrEP line: (210) 207-7292. Counseling line (210) 207-2816, Mon-Thu 8-4:30, Fri 8-12.

records.name: San Antonio Metro Health WIC
records.description_en: WIC gives healthy food benefits, nutrition classes, and breastfeeding support to moms and young kids at 10 clinics around San Antonio.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Pregnant, postpartum, and breastfeeding women, infants, and children younger than 5.
records.how_to_apply: Call 3-1-1 or (210) 207-6000, or contact the nearest WIC clinic.
records.hours: Most clinics 7:45 a.m.-4:30 p.m. weekdays, some evenings until 7:30 p.m.; close 12:45 p.m. Fridays; limited Saturday hours; closed the first Friday of each month
records.notes: Address shown is Buena Vista clinic (210-207-4906). Other clinics: Callaghan 4412 Callaghan Rd 78228 (210-207-4694); Grissom 9179 Grissom Rd Ste 147 78251 (210-207-4754); Marbach 7452 Military Dr W 78227 (210-207-4690); Naco-Perrin 4020 Naco-Perrin 78217 (210-207-4742); Pecan Valley 802 Pecan Valley 78220 (210-207-4715); Rittiman 4343 Rittiman Rd 78218 (210-207-4750); Salinas 630 S General McMullen 78237 (210-207-4700); South Flores 6723 S Flores #106 78221 (210-207-4555); Zarzamora 4503 S Zarzamora 78211 (210-207-4720). CentroMed and CommuniCare also run WIC.

records.name: Child Care Services (Child Care Scholarships)
records.description_en: Helps pay for child care so parents can work or go to school or training. Families choose from a network of over 500 approved providers.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Parents in the 13-county Alamo region who are working or in training and meet program income rules.
records.how_to_apply: Apply for a child care scholarship through Texas Child Care Connection online. Call (210) 230-6300 for help.
records.notes: Toll-free (800) 204-7905; email ccs@wsalamo.org. Region also includes Atascosa, Bandera, Frio, Gillespie, Karnes, Kendall, Kerr, McMullen, Medina and Wilson counties. Income limits are set on the state portal.

records.name: Workforce Solutions Alamo Career Centers
records.description_en: Free job search help, resume and interview help, hiring events, and training for in-demand jobs like IT, construction, and healthcare.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Job seekers in the 13-county Alamo region, including Bexar, Comal, and Guadalupe counties.
records.how_to_apply: Register on WorkInTexas.com and visit a local career center, or call (210) 224-4357 to find the nearest center.
records.notes: Address is the administrative office, not a career center. Center locations: https://www.workforcesolutionsalamo.org/workforce-career-locations/. Main admin line (210) 438-0581. Also offers vocational rehabilitation services.

records.name: Youth Empowerment Services (YES)
records.description_en: Helps young people finish school, get paid work experience, job training, mentoring, and money skills.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Youth ages 16-24 who face barriers to school, training, or work and meet program rules.
records.how_to_apply: Apply online or go to a free weekly info session (Mon-Fri 2:00 PM at career centers, or online Fridays 10:00 AM). Call (210) 224-4357 or text (210) 457-2366.
records.notes: Email yes@wsalamo.org. No registration needed for info sessions.

records.name: Veteran Employment Services
records.description_en: Job placement, training, resume help, and priority service for veterans. Some military spouses can also get help.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Veterans in the 13-county Alamo region. Military spouses who lost a job due to relocation or are unemployed/underemployed may also qualify.
records.how_to_apply: Call (210) 224-4357 or email veteranservices@wsalamo.org, or visit any career center.
records.notes: Military Family Support Program: (210) 745-8695, MFSP@wsalamo.org.

records.name: City of San Antonio Head Start and Early Head Start
records.organization: City of San Antonio Department of Human Services
records.description_en: Free early learning and child care programs for babies, toddlers, and preschoolers.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Children 6 weeks to 5 years old. Early Head Start is for 6 weeks to 35 months; Head Start is for ages 3-5.
records.how_to_apply: Apply online through the ChildPlus application in English or Spanish, or call (210) 206-5500.
records.notes: Separate applications for Edgewood ISD (210-898-2043) and San Antonio ISD (210-554-2410) programs. Income rules not stated on the page.

records.name: Head Start and Early Head Start (Comal & Guadalupe)
records.organization: Community Council of South Central Texas
records.description_en: Early learning programs for babies, toddlers, and preschoolers from low-income families.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Low-income families with children from birth to age 5 in Comal and Guadalupe counties.
records.how_to_apply: Apply online or call (830) 327-4990.

records.name: After School Challenge
records.organization: City of San Antonio Department of Human Services
records.description_en: After-school program at elementary schools with homework help, tutoring, and fun activities.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Elementary students at participating school sites. Fees are based on family income and size.
records.how_to_apply: Contact your child's school or the program office for your school district.
records.cost: Sliding scale based on family income, size, and number of children
records.notes: District contacts: Edgewood ISD (210) 229-7827; Harlandale ISD (210) 436-0686; San Antonio ISD (210) 554-2605; South San ISD (210) 433-9922; Southwest ISD (210) 622-4335.

records.name: Project QUEST
records.description_en: Career training in healthcare, trades/manufacturing, and IT, with tuition help, emergency financial support, and one-on-one career coaching.
records.eligibility_summary_en: San Antonio-area adults who want training for a new career. Call or attend an info session to check eligibility.
records.how_to_apply: Sign up for a free virtual or in-person information session, then apply through the services page. Call (210) 630-4607 with questions.
records.notes: Alternate phone (210) 630-4619. Eligibility rules not listed on the homepage.

records.name: San Antonio Ready to Work
records.organization: City of San Antonio Workforce Development Office
records.description_en: Pays tuition for approved job training and college courses, with coaching and emergency help for rent, utilities, child care, food, and transportation while you train.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Adults 18+ living inside San Antonio city limits who can work in the U.S. and have income at or below 250% of the federal poverty level.
records.how_to_apply: Apply online, call 3-1-1, or visit a Ready to Work partner agency.
records.notes: Residents of suburban cities outside San Antonio limits do not qualify. Bachelor's degree holders can earn credentials but not tuition for degree programs.

records.name: Texas RioGrande Legal Aid - San Antonio
records.description_en: Free civil legal help with housing and evictions, public benefits, family law, employment, education, taxes, wills, and disaster issues.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Low-income people in TRLA's 68-county service area, which includes Bexar, Comal, and Guadalupe counties. Call to see if you qualify.
records.how_to_apply: Call the intake line at (956) 996-8752 or toll-free (833) 329-8752, Monday-Friday 9 a.m.-5 p.m. Family law calls are taken Tuesdays and Thursdays only.
records.notes: Intake also at (956) 996-8752. No dedicated New Braunfels or Seguin office listed; those counties are served from the regional network. TRLA publishes an eviction toolkit.

records.name: Tenant/Landlord Mediation and Fair Housing Counseling
records.organization: City of San Antonio Neighborhood & Housing Services Department
records.description_en: Free help from HUD-certified housing counselors to settle problems with a landlord, like repairs, deposits, lease disputes, utilities, and evictions.
records.eligibility_summary_en: San Antonio tenants and landlords with a housing dispute. Counselors are not lawyers and do not give legal advice.
records.notes: Housing discrimination complaints: https://www.sa.gov/Directory/Departments/NHSD/Housing-Support/Counseling-Mediation/Discrimination-Complaints

records.name: Eviction Prevention Help
records.organization: City of San Antonio Neighborhood & Housing Services Department
records.description_en: The city answers eviction questions, shares tenant rights guides, and connects renters to rent and utility help.
records.eligibility_summary_en: San Antonio renters facing eviction or behind on rent.
records.how_to_apply: Call (210) 207-5910 or use the eviction help online form on the city website.
records.notes: Other rent/utility help listed by the city: Bexar County Housing Authority (210) 225-0071; Catholic Charities (utilities) (210) 226-6171; Christian Assistance Ministry (210) 223-4099; Salvation Army (210) 352-2020; St. Vincent de Paul (210) 225-7837.

records.name: City of San Antonio Rental Assistance Program
records.organization: City of San Antonio Neighborhood & Housing Services Department
records.description_en: Helps renters with a hardship pay up to 3 months of rent (up to $3,500) and utilities (up to $1,500).
records.eligibility_summary_en: San Antonio city renters (Council Districts 1-10) with household income at or below 80% of Area Median Income and a financial hardship. Once per 12 months.
documents_needed: Photo ID for adults; birth certificates for children
Social Security cards for household members who have them
Current lease
Proof of income for the last 60 days
Proof of hardship (job loss, reduced hours, medical bills, etc.)
Notice to vacate or eviction citation, if you have one
records.how_to_apply: Apply online on the second Wednesday of each month; the portal is open from 1 p.m. to 2 p.m. Call (210) 207-6459 or 3-1-1 for help.
records.hours: Application portal: second Wednesday of each month, 1 p.m. - 2 p.m.
records.notes: Limit is based on Area Median Income, not FPL (2026 80% AMI: $56,350 for 1 person up to $106,300 for 8). Asset documents needed if savings/investments exceed $5,000.

records.name: City of San Antonio Utility Assistance
records.organization: City of San Antonio Department of Human Services
records.description_en: Helps low-income San Antonio households pay their CPS Energy bill.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Households with income at or below 150% of the federal poverty level. Priority for families with children under 17, people with disabilities, and seniors 60+.
documents_needed: Photo ID and last 4 digits of the account holder's Social Security number
Proof of residency and legal status for household members
Proof of income for the last 30 days for all adults
CPS Energy bill and account number
records.how_to_apply: Apply online or visit the Willie Velasquez Learning Center. Call (210) 207-8198 with questions. Processing can take 30 days or more.
records.notes: This is the local CEAP-type utility program for San Antonio.

records.name: Utility Assistance (CEAP) - Comal & Guadalupe
records.organization: Community Council of South Central Texas
records.description_en: Helps low-income households pay electric and gas bills. Help can be up to $1,800 depending on income.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Households at or below 150% of the federal poverty level in the service area, including Comal and Guadalupe counties. Priority for seniors 60+, people with disabilities, and families with children under 5.
records.how_to_apply: Follow the apply instructions on the website and email your application to your county office, or call (830) 767-2019.
records.notes: Up to $1,800 (0-50% FPL), $1,500 (51-75%), $1,200 (76-150%). Program contact address on the page is 1220 Simmons Ave, Jourdanton; Seguin address is the agency location. Also offers weatherization and rental help.

records.name: VIA Reduced Fare Program
records.description_en: Lower bus fares for seniors, students, children, people with disabilities, disabled veterans, active military, and Medicare/SSDI recipients.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Seniors 62+, students 12+, children 5-13, people with certain disabilities, veterans with a disability rating, active-duty military, and Medicare or SSDI recipients.
documents_needed: Seniors: government photo ID with birth date
Students: proof of registration or tuition payment
Disability: completed Reduced Fare Application (veterans: VA disability papers)
Medicare/SSDI: Medicare card, government ID, and/or SSDI award letter
records.how_to_apply: Get a Reduced Fare ID at any VIA Information Center (except Randolph Transit Center). Call (210) 362-2020 for help.
records.cost: Reduced fare; seniors 62+ pay 25 cents weekdays 9 a.m.-3 p.m. and ride free on weekends; children 4 and under ride free
records.notes: Students may apply online.

records.name: Haven for Hope
records.organization: Haven for Hope of Bexar County
records.description_en: A campus for people experiencing homelessness with a low-barrier shelter, street and jail outreach, and longer-term support services.
records.eligibility_summary_en: People experiencing homelessness in San Antonio/Bexar County. Contact intake for requirements.
records.how_to_apply: Go to the campus or call (210) 220-2100 and ask about intake.
records.notes: South Campus is a low-barrier shelter; North Campus offers transformational services with an average 50-day stay. Intake hours not stated on the page.
